finding.claim: OS command injection: the unauthenticated /ping endpoint concatenates the user-controlled `host` query parameter into a shell command string run via exec(), allowing arbitrary command execution (e.g. host=127.0.0.1;id or $(...)). Output is also returned to the caller, so results are directly exfiltrable.
finding.sink: child_process.exec("ping -c 1 " + req.query.host) at tools.js:7, executed via /bin/sh

trace.note: Route handler for GET /ping, no auth middleware
req.query.host concatenated directly into shell command passed to exec()
Command stdout returned in response, enabling output exfiltration

finding.guards_checked: No input validation, allowlist, or escaping of host; no authentication/authorization middleware; no use of execFile with argument array; no express middleware registered. Query param could also be an array/object (qs parsing) but string concatenation still yields injection.

verdict.reason: tools.js:7 passes "ping -c 1 " + req.query.host to exec() (run via /bin/sh) with no validation, auth middleware, or escaping, and tools.js:11 returns stdout. With host=127.0.0.1;id the shell exit status is that of `id` (0), so the output is sent to the anonymous caller.

verdict_facts.reason: tools.js:7 passes "ping -c 1 " + req.query.host to exec() (a shell) with no validation, and the route at tools.js:6 has no auth, so an anonymous caller can inject commands such as `;id`, and tools.js:11 returns stdout when the command succeeds.
